name: Arctic Open
stakes: This Super 500 event offers India's top shuttlers a crucial opportunity to consolidate their form, chase individual titles, and gather valuable ranking points following the intensity of the Asian Games.
summary:
India's shuttlers arrive at the Arctic Open, a Super 500 event, looking to build on—or rebound from—their recent Asian Games campaign. The men's team delivered a commendable performance, securing a bronze medal after a hard-fought semifinal loss to defending champions China. Key players like Lakshya Sen, Ayush Shetty, and the formidable men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty were instrumental in this historic achievement, marking India's second badminton medal in the Games' history.

On the women's side, the campaign ended in the quarter-finals with a 1-3 defeat to Japan. While PV Sindhu led the charge, only the promising women's doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand managed to secure a win in that tie. With no specific draws announced for the Arctic Open yet, the Indian contingent will be eager to translate their team event experiences into strong individual showings in Finland.
